messages:
jana: noticing a p99 jump on prod-serving pool B ~ 1834507800-1834507880 window, correlated with some long prompts + tool calls. stack traces look like kernel fallback + big KV refill. any quick ideas?

miguel: saw the alert, looking. initial tail distribution looks like a bi-modal — most <120ms but a small mass at 1.2s+. :eyes:

ryan: can you paste the aggregate trace? microbatch sizes and kernel chosen?

jana: pasted sampling from logs below (scrubbed ids):

```
# sample request meta
seq_len: 1024, prompt_tokens: 950, tool_calls: 2, cold_kv: true, microbatch: 4, kernel: auto-select->xform_optim_fallback
latency: 1.26s p99, p50 95ms
trace: kv_fetch(820ms) -> kernel_switch(120ms) -> generate(200ms)
```

miguel: that kv_fetch 820ms is alarming. is that disk-backed? which cache tier?

jana: it looks like a mix: hot key cache had misses and we fell back to remote KVS over RDMA, not local GPU shared cache. also saw a lot of small tool-call RPCs that block token stream.

aisha: are we seeing any microbatching knob differences? microbatch 4 seems standard, but with long prompts and tool-calls we might nurse multiple cache misses into one request.

ryan: two hypotheses: (1) long prompt causes large KV reads that overflow our GPU-side cache causing remote fetches, (2) tool-calls create repeated syscalls that stall the runtime scheduling and prevent batching from amortizing kernel startup.

perf-ci-bot: perf-regression check: recent kernel selection change (CL #8241) rolled 48h ago, 6% p99 worse on long-context regression tests.

miguel: thanks bot. CL8241 changed our kernel scoring heuristic to prefer fused kernels for throughput — might increase init cost for long sequences.

jana: so combined effect: kernel preference -> heavier init on large sequences, kv misses -> remote fetch latency, tool-calls -> serializing execution. that aligns with observed stack.

aisha: quick mitigation: route requests with prompt_tokens>800 to low-latency pool with warmer KV and conservative kernel choices. we can do an emergency routing rule for next 6 hours. thoughts?

ryan: +1 for routing. also suggest temporary microbatch reduction to 1 for those requests so they don't wait for microbatch handshake and we avoid mixing with small short requests. tradeoff: lower throughput.

miguel: agree. also we should toggle kernel-selection ablation flag to pre-CL behavior for pool B to confirm causality. set kernel.selection_mode=legacy for canary.

jana: I'll push routing rule and microbatch override. patch outline:

```
route.if prompt_tokens > 800 => pool: lowlat-pool-b, microbatch:1, kernel_flag: legacy
```

aisha: add kv.prefetch=true for that route to warm GPU KV cache when request is accepted. prefetch should reduce remote RTTs.

perf-ci-bot: benchmark note: prefetching increases average CPU usage but can drop tail by ~30-50% in sims for long-context flows.

ryan: after we patch, can we also capture stackprof on a few hits? need to confirm kernel init time vs kv fetch. add debug sampling header X-Trace-Sample: 1/100.

jana: patch deployed to staging, routing + microbatch override + kv.prefetch enabled. will monitor. :crossed_fingers:

(30m later)

jana: quick update — p99 dropped from 1.26s -> 240ms on the affected pool for sampled requests. throughput for that pool dropped ~8% overall.

miguel: good signal that routing + microbatch helped. can we rollback kernel ablation now to compare?

aisha: rolled kernel.selection_mode back to legacy on canary; comparing traces shows kernel init delta ~110ms for these long sequences. KV fetch still contributed ~120-150ms after prefetch in the warm path.

ryan: so root causes ranked: (1) KV cold misses on long prompts, (2) kernel init penalty from recent heuristic change, (3) tool-call-induced serialization. All three compound to create the long tail.

jana: next steps:
- make route permanent for >800 tokens while we improve caching
- revert kernel heuristic and re-run benchmark with real requests + perf harness
- add prefetch + async tool-call handling (non-blocking tool invocation) prototype
- create a microbatching doc describing when to force batch=1 for latency SLOs

miguel: I'll own the kernel heuristic revert and perf runs. ryan can you prototype async tool-call scheduling? jana please own routing + SRE runbook.

ryan: will prototype non-blocking tool-call flow + add metrics for tool-call blocking time.

ops-bot: incident note created: INC-2026-314, assigned eng-runtime, priority P2.

jana: adding a quick snippet for the runbook we used:

```
Runbook excerpt:
1) Identify spike window and affected pool
2) Check perf-ci for recent kernel changes
3) If long-context heavy: route prompt_tokens>800 to lowlat pool with microbatch=1
4) Enable kv.prefetch and sample 1% traces
5) If kernel deltas present: toggle kernel.selection_mode=legacy on canary
6) Monitor p95/p99, rollback when stable
```

aisha: nice. can we add an automated alert that triggers when p99 > 500ms AND >0.5% of requests have prompt_tokens>800? automated routing could flip faster.

jana: filed FR: FR-872 add auto-routing by tail-profile. linking in the ticket.

miguel: thanks all. lessons: long prompts need explicit cache strategy + careful kernel init accounting; microbatch heuristics can hurt latency under skewed request mixes. closing thread after postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
